title: Nicolas Cage Says He’s ‘Probably Not’ Working With Amazon Again After Refusing to Sign AI Waiver for ‘Spider-Noir,’ Teases Joining ‘True Detective’
key_facts: Nicolas Cage spoke on the Empire Stage panel at New York Comic Con on Saturday (10 Oct 2026).
Variety says Amazon, which developed “Spider-Noir” for Prime Video, allegedly asked Cage to sign an AI waiver; Cage says he did not sign it.
Cage said he is “probably not going to be working with that studio again, but that’s okay.”
Cage said Amazon has invested $50 billion in OpenAI (his figure, not Variety's).
Amazon canceled the series after one season last month, days before the Emmys, where it had 11 nominations, the most of any Prime Video program this year.
The series drew 2.6 billion minutes viewed in its first six weeks, per Variety.
Cage also said his next project is a season of HBO’s “True Detective”; HBO did not immediately respond to Variety.
quote_evidence: Nicolas Cage is speaking out against Amazon after the company, which developed “Spider-Noir” for Prime Video, allegedly asked him to sign an AI waiver.

Amazon canceled the superhero series after just one season last month, days before the first weekend of the Emmy Awards, where it had earned 11 nominations (the most of any Prime Video program this year).
HBO did not immediately respond to request for comment on Cage’s participation on “True Detective.”
why_it_matters_hint: A leading actor publicly links a refused AI waiver to the end of his relationship with a major studio, a rare on-record case of an actor declining AI consent terms.
event_date: 10 Oct 2026 (panel at New York Comic Con)
notes: Full Variety text read. The waiver claim is Cage's account; Variety reports no Amazon comment. The cancellation of the series (September 2026) is background, not today's news. True Detective claim unconfirmed by HBO.
